redistricting.sourceNote: State statuses are maintained locally so stale public rating feeds do not silently drive the House model after mid-decade map changes.

AL.note: Alabama's request to revert to its 2023 congressional map was blocked on May 26, 2026; the court map remains the baseline while appeals continue.
AL.source: NCSL mid-decade tracker; AP/Axios May 2026 coverage

CA.note: California's Proposition 50 map is treated as the 2026 baseline.

FL.note: Florida enacted a new 2026 congressional map; state litigation remains a watch item.

GA.note: Georgia's official redistricting steps are for 2028, not the 2026 House election.

IN.note: Indiana lawmakers voted down new maps; current maps remain in effect for 2026.

LA.note: Louisiana enacted Act 2 / SB 121 on May 29, 2026 after Louisiana v. Callais; the model forces a 5R-1D seat-rating baseline until public rating feeds fully catch up.
LA.source: Louisiana Legislature SB121; Louisiana redistricting files; AP May 29, 2026

MD.note: Maryland redistricting legislation died; no new 2026 congressional map is modeled.

MO.note: Missouri's 2025 map is modeled as active while referendum and signature litigation continue.

NC.note: North Carolina's October 2025 congressional map is treated as active for 2026.

NY.note: A state court redraw order was stayed and dismissed; current New York maps remain in effect.

OH.note: Ohio's October 2025 map is treated as active for 2026.

SC.note: South Carolina redistricting legislation died in the Senate; 2022 congressional maps remain the 2026 baseline.

TN.note: Tennessee's May 2026 congressional map is treated as active for 2026.

UT.note: Utah's court-adopted 2025 map is treated as active for 2026.

WA.note: Washington's redistricting proposal died; no new 2026 congressional map is modeled.
